name: Morse Hall
use: Institute for the Study of Earth, Oceans, and Space (EOS) research labs and offices
builtText: 1984–86 (federal grant 1983; occupied 1986; dedicated Aug 19, 1992); archives index says 1985
style: 1980s postmodern brick research building with glazed entrance pavilion and columns
statusNote: Building-wide HVAC and envelope renewal under way

renovations.what: Capital project under way: replace building-wide HVAC (primary systems 38 years old), improve envelope (doors, window sealant, skylight), modernize original fume hoods; CM-at-risk

facts.text: A $15 million federal grant was awarded in 1983 after a 1982 proposal to Senator Warren Rudman; groundbreaking 1984, occupied 1986.
Dedicated August 19, 1992 to trustee Richard A. Morse (class of 1951).
UNH Facilities says lab spaces cannot hold the temperature and humidity tolerances research grants require, and the original fume hoods are in poor condition.
EOS has its director's office at 305 Morse Hall, 8 College Road.

verdict: 1986 postmodern brick research block for EOS with a columned glass entry; its labs can't hold the conditions research grants demand.
notes: Photos (2013) show a 1980s tan-and-red brick block with banding, a columned glazed entrance bay and a skylight/atrium element; the long side is plain with dumpsters and a service door. A/C marked partial because HVAC exists but cannot hold lab tolerances. Old row said "Mathematics" also housed here: not confirmed (admissions blog calls Kingsbury the math building). A $11.5M Morse HVAC budget appears in USNH ICPC minutes (March 2026) per search excerpt but the PDF could not be read; unconfirmed. Architect unknown. No student sentiment found.
judgeNotes: Photos show a decent entrance and a plain service side. Condition 3 on Facilities' own assessment (38-year-old HVAC, poor fume hoods).
